VOREC Community Grant Program

The VOREC Community Grant Program (VCGP) is intended to fund community projects that support and grow local economies by leveraging outdoor recreation. 

  • Current status: 2027 grant round is now open. Pre-Application materials are due December 13, 2026
  • Eligible applicants: Municipalities, non-profit organizations and other governmental entities
  • Funding source: One-time State General Funds, Vermont Recreational Trails Fund 
  • Total funds available: $285,000+

The Vermont Outdoor Recreation Economic Collaborative (VOREC) Community Grant Program, also known as VCGP, supports outdoor recreation projects that drive economic growth and enhance community well-being. Funded by one-time allocations by the Vermont General Assembly, this is the fifth VCGP grant round.  

In order to maximize the impact of the available funding, the upcoming grant round will focus on project development and promotion. This grant will fund projects that will support local outdoor recreation economies, but need design, scoping, or planning work done to unlock other funding. This program will also help communities and organizations share information about their amazing recreation resources and businesses by supporting marketing, branding, and other promotion.  

The grant round will be closely tied to the vision, common objectives, and themes of Move Forward Together Vermont. The scoring system will be designed to elevate projects that address equity and climate resilience.

2027 Grant Round Anticipated Timeline  

  • Pre-applications open and application materials released by Tuesday, October 6, 2026   
  • Pre-application submission deadline:  Sunday, December 13, 2026  
  • Full application submission deadline: Wednesday, February 17, 2027  
  • Grant application review and selection: mid-February – late March 2027   
  • Compliance reviews and grant agreement development: April – June 2027  
  • Anticipated project implementation period: July 1, 2027 - December 31, 2028 

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicant Eligibility 

Eligible applicants will include municipalities and nonprofits. New grantees will be prioritized, but previous successful grantees will still be eligible to apply. Current VCGP grantees with active grants as of Dec 13, 2026, will not be eligible. 

Project Eligibility 

Example eligible projects that might score well could include:   

  • Contracting a landscape architect to complete a park design for a FEMA buyout property   
  • Creating a regional outdoor recreation marketing plan to attract outdoor recreationists to downtown businesses   
  • Community-informed planning for both building and sharing information about accessible trails   
  • Program development for classes or community events focused on building confidence in the outdoors    
  • Creating a town-wide outdoor recreation wayfinding plan and installing signs/kiosks using accessible signage principles   
  • Developing a community economic recovery plan focused on supporting local businesses, and outdoor recreation resources following emergencies and natural disasters.    
  • Developing a climate risk mitigation plan and preparing permit applications for identified trail improvement projects. 

All projects must be successfully completed within the designated implementation period. 

Award and Match Requirements 

Grant amounts will range from $7,500 recommended minimum to $50,000 maximum.  Holding true to VCGP history, no match will be required.  

This round will be supplemented by Vermont Recreational Trail Funds. This portion of the funding will be available only to trail planning projects, due to statutory funding constraints.

Reimbursement Requirements 

VCGP is a reimbursement program, and grantees must be capable of financing the project and (after a grant agreement is fully executed) first paying for expenditures and then submitting a request to the State for reimbursement using the required documentation. 

Application Process and Resources 

To apply for VCGP funding, there is a two-step application process that begins with a short pre-application submission. Pre-application submissions will be reviewed for compliance with the VCGP program. Selected applicants will then be invited to submit a proposal for full review.   

How to Submit a Pre-Application 

Pre-application submissions will close at 11:59 PM on December 13, 2026. Email all of following required documents to ANR.FPRRecreationGrants@vermont.gov by the deadline to submit a pre-application: 

  • VCGP Pre-Application Form 
  • VCGP Workplan 
  • VCGP Budget 

Pre-applications must include all of the required documents. Grants staff will screen submissions received before 5 pm on Wednesday, December 9, for completeness and notify applicants of any missing documentation that still needs to be submitted by 11:59 pm on Sunday, December 13, 2026. 

For proposals submitted after 5 pm on December 9, applicants are strongly encouraged to carefully review their email submission to ensure all required materials are submitted by the deadline as incomplete proposals will not be considered for moving to the Full Application stage. 

How to Submit a Full Application  

If invited to submit a full proposal, the full grant application will be offered through the ANROnline portal. To complete your full grant application, you will need to follow the steps below. 

  1. Download, review, and complete all other required templates and supplemental materials for your project. 

  1. Complete the 2027 VCGP Grant Application Form and submit it online.
